newsitem.title: USA: Blue chip stocks power ahead; Dow index just short of record.
newsitem.headline: Blue chip stocks power ahead; Dow index just short of record.

text.p: Blue chip stocks powered higher on Thursday, bouncing back strongly from three straight sessions of lower closes as the mood on Wall Street turned positive on news of record U.S. exports and a rise in weekly jobless claims.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 58.35 points at 7,777.06, standing just below its record closing high of 7,782.04 set on June 13.
The 30-stock blue chip index rallied briefly through 7,800 for the first time ever, peaking at 7,810.54 before settling back.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks and the NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks both set new highs.
In the broader market, advancing issues swamped declines 1,739 to 783 on active volume of 536 million on the New York Stock Exchange.
The market was also propelled by an upbeat forecast by Prudential Securities' well-known market bull, Ralph Acampora, who raised his targets for the Dow to 10,000 in the next year.

Investors were already cheering a narrower-than-expected April trade deficit and news that exports jumped to a record high, despite a strong dollar, as well as a surprising jump in weekly jobless claims. The developments were expected to deter the Federal Reserve from moving toward an interest rate rise at its policy-setting meeting in July.

"There's a lot of buying momentum out there. (Acampora) just keeps on increasing his numbers. That creates a very strong bullish feeling on Wall Street," said Warren Epstein, director of trading at Richard Rosenblatt.

Acampora, Prudential Securities' director of technical research, advised people to "Remain fully invested -- we expect the stock market to mount an explosive advance during the second half of the year," he wrote in a report.
Weekly jobless claims rose to 347,000 in the latest week from 339,000 a week earlier, suggesting that the red-hot labour market might be cooling.

The government also said the trade deficit rose 7.8 percent in April to $8.4 billion but noted that exports hit a record level. That could mean bigger profits ahead for U.S. companies who do business abroad, analysts said.

Traders said stocks also benefited from a burst of buying prior to Friday's "triple witching" expiration of futures and options. Some investors who had bet that stocks would fall had to cover their bets and buy them back, even in a rising market.
Stocks easily overcame a stronger-than-expected regional economic report. The Philadelphia Federal Reserve's June business activity index jumped to 25.2, sharply above expectations of a 7.3 reading.
Analysts chose to view the report as evidence that the economy might be in for a good robust third quarter without a rate hike by the Fed.

"When you see the market ignore bad news, that could mean something speculative or irrational is going on," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer for First Albany Corp. "It might be a clue that the inflow to mutual funds is so big, there's a great sense of urgency for portfolio managers to buy."
Tobacco and drugs were strong while oil and airline stocks fell.

The shares of tobacco makers rose as investors anticipated liability settlement talks could soon yield an agreement, traders said. Philip Morris Cos. and RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp. were the most heavily-traded stocks on the Big Board. Philip Morris added 2 to 47-1/2 and RJR rose 1-3/8 to 35-7/8.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 14.71 points to 1,447.14.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 8.93 points to 897.99, a new high. The American Stock Exchange index rose 2.33 to 628.30.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 4.35 to 467.76, a new high. The average share was up 41 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a new high of 8,484.158, up 84.986, or 1.01 percent.
